title: Descent of a connected open using a finite locally free multisection
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ and $p:Z\to B$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\sigma:Z\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=p$. Suppose that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and that every fibre $X_b$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(b)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Suppose that $p$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $b_0\in B$ satisfy $Z_{b_0}\ne\varnothing$ and suppose that $X_{b_0}$ is geometrically connected over $\kappa(b_0)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], where connected includes nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then there exists a quasi-compact open subscheme $X^0\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] such that $X^0_{b_0}=X_{b_0}$ as open subschemes of $X_{b_0}$ and every nonempty fibre of $X^0\to B$ is geometrically connected over its residue field [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Base change (f) and (sigma) along (p:Z\to B). Put (Y=X_Z=X\times_B Z), with its section (s:Z\to Y) induced by (sigma), and let (C=Y^0) be the union of the fibre connected components containing (s). Flatness and finite presentation pass to this base change by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3); geometric reducedness of fibres is preserved by the iterated field extension in the definition of geometric reducedness. Thus the new open-section-component lemma [lem-trf-flat-reduced-section-component-open] applies and (C) is open in (Y).

source.place: Tag 057I proof, formation of X_Z and application of lemma-connected-along-section-open

proof.text: Over (Z\times_B Z), the two pullbacks of (C) along the two projections are the component loci attached to the two induced sections. This is exactly the base-change compatibility of section-component loci [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian]. For every point of the fibre ((Z\times_B Z)_{b_0}), the two sections lie in the whole fibre (X_{b_0}), because that fibre is geometrically connected and the designated fibre of (Z) is nonempty. Since (p) is finite locally free, this fibre product fibre is finite; openness of the two component loci therefore gives an open neighbourhood (W) of ((Z\times_B Z)_{b_0}) on which each section image lies in the other component locus.

source.place: Tag 057I proof, paragraph beginning Let (Z ×_Y Z)_y = {z_1, …, z_n}

proof.text: The morphism (Z\times_B Z\to B) is finite locally free: each projection is a base change of (p), hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and their composite is finite locally free by [lem-trf-finite-locally-free-composition]. Its underlying map is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], so it is open and closed. Shrink to an affine open neighbourhood (V) of (b_0) whose inverse image is contained in (W). The image of (Z\to B) is also open and closed by the same two leaves, and so we shrink (V) further inside that image. Then (Z_V\to V) is finite locally free and surjective, hence an fpqc covering.

source.place: Tag 057I proof, paragraph using finite locally free hence open and closed

proof.text: On (Z_V\times_V Z_V), the two pullbacks of (C) are equal: the two inclusions established in (W) imply equality directly from the construction of the section component locus. The induced cover (X_{Z_V}\to X_V) is finite locally free by base-change permanence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), so it is fpqc. Apply fpqc descent of compatible open subschemes [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] to this cover. It gives a unique open (X^0\subseteq X_V) whose pullback to (X_{Z_V}) is (C|_{Z_V}).

source.place: Tag 057I proof, paragraph beginning After we do this we see that X_Z^0 …

proof.text: The component locus (C) is quasi-compact after the affine base shrink by [lem-trf-section-component-quasi-compact]. Since (X_{Z_V}\to X_V) is finite (base change of the finite map (Z_V\to V)), the descended open (X^0), whose inverse image is (C), is quasi-compact: its underlying image is the continuous image of the quasi-compact space (C), and the fpqc descent equality identifies that image with (X^0).

source.place: Tag 057I proof, final paragraph on quasi-compactness

proof.text: At (b_0), the pullback of (C) is the whole (X_{Z_{b_0}}), since (X_{b_0}) is geometrically connected. Faithfully flat base change along the nonempty fibre (Z_{b_0}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b_0)) therefore gives (X^0_{b_0}=X_{b_0}). For any (b\in V), after a field extension to a point of (Z_b), the fibre of (X^0) is a connected component containing the section point; [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes it geometrically connected. The converse direction of [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension] descends geometric connectedness from that field extension to the residue field of b. Thus every nonempty fibre of (X^0\to V) is geometrically connected. Viewing (X_V) as an open subscheme of (X) proves the claimed open (X^0\subseteq X).
